RE: FOIL Records Request of January 11, 2025, Reference # R000023-011125 
Dear Matthew Fecteau, 
The NYS Department of Financial Services received a FOIL request from you on January 11, 2025. You requested: "Pursuant to applicable laws and regulations, I am requesting access to any and all records, documents, and information related to First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company that are pertinent to assessing corporate governance, intercompany relationships, and financial practices. This request covers the period from January 1, 2018, to the date this request is processed (attached is an outdated but relevant document). Specifically, I seek: 

Corporate Governance and Structure: 

Organizational charts detailing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s relationship with its parent companies, including Reliance Standard Life Insurance, Delphi Financial Group, and Tokio Marine Holdings, and its affiliates. 
Board meeting minutes and resolutions involving First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its parent entities. 
Policies or communications governing decision-making processes, including approval of dividends or capital allocations. 
Financial Records: 

Records of intercompany loans, transfers, or payments involving First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its affiliates or parent companies. 
Financial statements, audits, or reports evidencing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s capitalization, reserves, and financial independence. 
Documentation on dividend payments made by First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company to its parent companies, including justification and impact on surplus reserves. 
Operational Independence: 

Service agreements, cost-sharing agreements, or contracts between First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and affiliated entities, such as claims management, IT services, and administrative support. 
Documents showing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s reinsurance arrangements, including agreements with affiliated or unaffiliated reinsurers. 
Compliance and Oversight: 

Correspondence with regulatory agencies, including the New York State Department of Financial Services, regarding First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s compliance with insurance regulations and financial standards. 
Internal audit reports or external reviews addressing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s operations, financial health, or governance. 
Shared Resources and Branding: 

Records or policies demonstrating shared resources, personnel, or branding between First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its parent companies or affiliates. 
Communications discussing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s operational independence or its role within the broader Tokio Marine Group. 
If certain records are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions along with a detailed explanation of the exemptions applied. I am willing to pay reasonable fees associated with fulfilling this request, but I request notification in advance if costs exceed a reasonable amount. 

Please send responsive documents electronically to my email address if possible. I appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response within the timeframe required by law." The New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) requires additional time to respond to your request, assigned the above Reference Number, because we are still working on your request. 
DFS will endeavor to provide you the determination of your FOIL request by August 15, 2025, or sooner if possible. However, if DFS is unable to complete its review by that time, you will then be provided an update on the progress of your FOIL request. Your continued patience is greatly appreciated. 
Sincerely, Lisa Derrick 
Administrative Specialist 
NYS Department of Financial Services 
Office of General Counsel

RE: FOIL Records Request of May 21, 2025, Reference # R000576-052125 
Dear Matthew Fecteau, 
The NYS Department of Financial Services received a FOIL request from you on May 21, 2025. You requested: "To Whom It May Concern: 
Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records: 
I am requesting access to all records in your possession from January 1, 2014, through the present concerning complaints, investigations, or regulatory actions involving Safety National Casualty Corporation, including any affiliated entities such as Safety Specialty Insurance Company and Sedgwick Claims Management Services, Inc. 
Specifically, I request copies of all consumer complaints alleging claim denials, delays, bad faith practices, misrepresentation of coverage, or failure to defend or indemnify insureds; any related correspondence or internal assessments; all regulatory enforcement actions, including market conduct examinations, administrative penalties, consent orders, fines, stipulations, or notices of violation; and any internal memoranda, emails, audit findings, or documentation regarding systemic or repeated misconduct. I also seek any statistical reports, dashboards, or complaint trend summaries reflecting activity related to Safety National during this period. 
The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 
Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires. 
Sincerely, 
Matthew Fecteau

Office of General Counsel

RE: FOIL Records Request of January 11, 2025, Reference # R000023-011125 
Dear Matthew Fecteau, 
The NYS Department of Financial Services received a FOIL request from you on January 11, 2025. You requested: "Pursuant to applicable laws and regulations, I am requesting access to any and all records, documents, and information related to First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company that are pertinent to assessing corporate governance, intercompany relationships, and financial practices. This request covers the period from January 1, 2018, to the date this request is processed (attached is an outdated but relevant document). Specifically, I seek: 

Corporate Governance and Structure: 

Organizational charts detailing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s relationship with its parent companies, including Reliance Standard Life Insurance, Delphi Financial Group, and Tokio Marine Holdings, and its affiliates. 
Board meeting minutes and resolutions involving First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its parent entities. 
Policies or communications governing decision-making processes, including approval of dividends or capital allocations. 
Financial Records: 

Records of intercompany loans, transfers, or payments involving First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its affiliates or parent companies. 
Financial statements, audits, or reports evidencing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s capitalization, reserves, and financial independence. 
Documentation on dividend payments made by First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company to its parent companies, including justification and impact on surplus reserves. 
Operational Independence: 

Service agreements, cost-sharing agreements, or contracts between First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and affiliated entities, such as claims management, IT services, and administrative support. 
Documents showing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s reinsurance arrangements, including agreements with affiliated or unaffiliated reinsurers. 
Compliance and Oversight: 

Correspondence with regulatory agencies, including the New York State Department of Financial Services, regarding First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s compliance with insurance regulations and financial standards. 
Internal audit reports or external reviews addressing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s operations, financial health, or governance. 
Shared Resources and Branding: 

Records or policies demonstrating shared resources, personnel, or branding between First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company and its parent companies or affiliates. 
Communications discussing First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company’s operational independence or its role within the broader Tokio Marine Group. 
If certain records are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions along with a detailed explanation of the exemptions applied. I am willing to pay reasonable fees associated with fulfilling this request, but I request notification in advance if costs exceed a reasonable amount. 

Please send responsive documents electronically to my email address if possible. I appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response within the timeframe required by law." The New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) requires additional time to respond to your request, assigned the above Reference Number, because we are still working on your request. 
DFS will endeavor to provide you the determination of your FOIL request by December 15, 2025, or sooner if possible. However, if DFS is unable to complete its review by that time, you will then be provided an update on the progress of your FOIL request. Your continued patience is greatly appreciated. 
Sincerely, Lisa Derrick 
Administrative Specialist 
NYS Department of Financial Services 
Office of General Counsel

title: City of Newcastle Opioid Settlment Funds

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: City of Newcastle Opioid Settlment Funds
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in City of Newcastle. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

title: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) (Saint Joseph County Police)

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) (Saint Joseph County Police)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields or dates is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

title: Library Contract Request: Interfolio (Northern Arizona University)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Elsevier relating to the licensing of Interfolio;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, data processing agreements, and/or letters of intent; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Elsevier for faculty information system technology; and Assessment documentation including, but not limited to, the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT). 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Interfolio.

The scope of this request should encompass more than just direct contracts or renewals between the university and Elsevier; please incorporate all applicable agreements and supporting records facilitated through consortium entities like Lyrasis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Orlando D-FOIA

communications.subject: ICE FOIA Request 2020-ICFO-56999
communications.communication:
June 24, 2020 Andrew Free MuckRock News DEPT MR 95563 411A Highland Ave Somerville, MA 02144 RE:     ICE FOIA Case Number 2020-ICFO-56999  Dear Mr. Free: This acknowledges receipt of your June 15, 2020, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for all records created in response to the FOIA requests designated by ICE-assigned tracking numbers listed below on the dates indicated; (please see request for details).  Your request was received in this office on June 15, 2020. Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10- day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you care to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations as they apply to non-commercial requesters.  As a non-commercial requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free, as are the first two hours of search time, after which you will pay the per quarter-hour rate ($4.00 for clerical personnel, $7.00 for professional personnel, $10.25 for managerial personnel) of the searcher.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 
Your request has been assigned reference number 2020-ICFO-56999. Please refer to this identifier in any future correspondence. To check the status of an ICE FOIA/PA request, please visit . communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request: ICE META-FOIA
communications.communication:
Good morning, 

Thank you for providing these records. I hereby appeal the adequacy of the agency’s search and its withholdings. With regard to the search, there obvious additional emails included by reference in the materials ICE FOIA produced, but those emails are absent from the production. For instance, there is the discussion of a “re-tasking” of search responsibilities for Peter Edge’s emails to HSI, following that component’s conclusion that there were no HSI records and thus nothing for the component to do. There are repeated references to the need to follow up with the requester — specifically from OAQ — but no communications from ICE to the requester. There are also references to placing the FOIA process on hold pending those clarifications, but no record indicating such designation was assigned. The system of records for tracking and monitor these FOIA was clearly not searched—just emails. Please re-task adequate searches. 

I also appeal the agency’s block withholding of email domains. As the Department of Justice admitted on ICE’s behalf in November for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in Transgender Law Center v. ICE, there is not a single case anywhere in the country finding email domains enjoy any cognizable privacy interest. 

Finally, I seek expedited processing of this appeal. The records produced indicate ICE FOIA violated federal law in multiple ways. First, ICE violated FOIA’s promptly available timing provisions. Second, ICE apparently mislead the administrative appeals body in the appeal of the Peter Edge FOIA by failing to notify that body that additional searches tasked to HSI were never conducted. Finally, ICE OAQ apparently violated the FOIA’s search requirements by placing a ‘hold’ on documents without ever following up with the requestor. I hereby certify the foregoing is true and correct pursuant to 28 USC 1746 and request expedited processing of the appeal pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e). 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal. 

Best regards, 

Andrew Free

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICAP-00440, 2022-ICAP-00463 

Dear Requester: 

The Department of Homeland Security has received your letter appealing the adverse determination of your Freedom of Information Act/Privacy Act (FOIA/PA) request by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Your appeal, dated on 8/15/2025, was received on 8/29/2025. 

The Government Information Law Division acknowledges your appeal request of and is assigning it number 2025-ICAP-00440 for tracking purposes.  Please reference this number in any future communications about your appeal. 

A high number of FOIA/PA requests have been received by the Department.  Accordingly, we have adopted the court-sanctioned practice of generally handling backlogged appeals on a first-in, first-out basis.   While we will make every effort to process your appeal on a timely basis, there may be some delay in resolving this matter.  Should you have any questions concerning the processing of your appeal, please contact Daniel Edgington ICE FOIA Office/Public Liaison at (866) 633-1182 or at 500 12th St., SW Washington, DC 20536-5009.
